findings.title: Slots inside a date override bypass the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, when a slot's date matches a date override and the slot falls inside the override window, the code hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` and returns before evaluating the `busy` array. That means for any host that has a date override on a given day, existing ACCEPTED bookings and external calendar events that fall inside the override window are completely ignored, and those slots are returned as available. An attendee can then book over an existing booking (double booking / data integrity). The busy check must still run for slots that lie within a date override; only the working-hours check should be skipped for override days.

findings.title: Working-hours check treats days outside the host's schedule as available
findings.body: The new working-hours filter uses `workingHours.find((workingHour) => { if (workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())) { ... } })`. If the slot's weekday is not included in any of the host's working-hours entries (e.g. a Saturday slot for a Mon-Fri host), the callback returns undefined for every entry, `find` returns undefined, and the code falls through to the busy-only check — i.e. the slot is considered available. For round-robin events the aggregate availability is the union of hosts, so slots generated from another host's Saturday availability will pass this fixed-host check even though the fixed host never works that day. A day with no matching working-hours entry must be treated as unavailable, not available.

findings.title: `end` is a duplicate of `start`, so slots overrunning the host's working hours are not rejected
findings.body: In the new working-hours check, `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start` and never accounts for the event length (it should be derived from slotEndTime). As a result the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` only rejects slots that *start* after the working hours end; a slot that starts before closing but extends past it (e.g. a 60-minute event starting 30 minutes before the fixed host's end of day) passes the check and is offered even though the host is not available for the full duration. This is precisely the class of bug (fixed hosts bookable when unavailable in round-robin) that this PR claims to fix, so the fix is undermined for end-of-day slots.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === , so the equal-start/end override branch is dead code
findings.body: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two Dayjs object references, which is always false regardless of the underlying times. The intended check — detecting overrides where start equals end (the "unavailable" full-day marker) — never executes, and such overrides instead fall through to the window comparisons, where a slot starting exactly at the override timestamp is returned as available. Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `.valueOf()`/`.getTime()`.

findings.title: Override date is formatted in the server's local timezone but compared against a UTC date
findings.body: The date gate compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` with `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. `slotStartTime` is `time.utc()` (UTC mode), but `dayjs(date.start)` is in the server's local timezone, so its `.format()` renders the date in the server's timezone. On any deployment where the process timezone is not UTC, the two dates disagree for times near midnight, causing date overrides to fail to match (slots wrongly unavailable via the fall-through, or wrongly available). The left side should be built with `dayjs.utc(date.start)` so both dates are rendered in UTC.

findings.title: Optional override.timeZone silently falls back to the server's local timezone
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` uses the new optional `timeZone` field of TimeRange. If a caller supplies date overrides without `timeZone` (the type explicitly allows this), `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` falls back to the server's local timezone, and the computed organizer UTC offset — and therefore every converted override start/end — will be wrong with no error. getSlots already receives `organizerTimeZone` as a parameter; that should be the fallback (or the field should be required) so a missing value cannot silently corrupt slot times.

findings.title: Overrides shifted across midnight by the timezone conversion are applied to the wrong invitee day
findings.body: activeOverrides is selected by checking `dayjs.utc(override.start)` (the raw stored wall-clock-UTC value) against the invitee's day window, but the override times are then converted to invitee-local minutes-of-day. When the offset shift moves the override across a midnight boundary, those minutes belong to a different calendar day than the one being built. Example: an organizer in UTC+13 with an override stored at 23:00–23:30 UTC and an invitee in UTC-11 yields an offset of -1440 minutes; the invitee-local times are 23:00–23:30 on the *previous* day, but the filter attaches the override to the invitee day containing the stored 23:00 UTC, so availability is added on the wrong day (and the user's normal working hours for the wrong day are removed).

findings.title: No test for the headline fix: round-robin with a fixed host having a date override
findings.body: The PR description states the primary fix is that date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events (issue #8207), but no test covers that scenario: all team-event tests use empty `hosts` or non-fixed configurations, and the only new test added is the timezone variant of a single-user personal event (which also only differs by 30 minutes of offset, both on the same side of the override window). Additionally, there is no test combining a date override with an existing booking, which is exactly the interaction that the new `dateOverrideExist` short-circuit in checkIfIsAvailable gets wrong (slots inside an override are never checked against busy times). Both scenarios should be covered before merging.
